sentences.text: Hello, and welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
My name is Emily.
I am happy you are here.
Today, we will talk about Serbia.
Serbia is a country with rivers, mountains,
and rich traditions in Southeast Europe.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Are you ready?
Let's begin.
Where is Serbia?
Serbia is in Southeastern Europe, in the Balkans.
It is next to Hungary, Romania, Bulgaria,
North Macedonia, Croatia, Bosnia, and Herzegovina,
and Montenegro.
It is a landlocked country, which means it has no sea.
What is the capital city of Serbia?
The capital city is Belgrade.
Belgrade is a large historic and lively city.
It sits at the meeting point of two rivers, the Danube and the Sava.
Belgrade has old buildings, modern life, and many cafes.
Other cities include Novi Sad, known for music and culture.
How many people live in Serbia?
About six.
Six million people live in Serbia.
Most people live in cities and towns,
but some live in villages in the countryside.
What language do people speak in Serbia?
The official language is Serbian.
It can be written in two alphabets, Latin and Cyrillic.
Many people also speak English, Hungarian, Bosnian, or Romani,
depending on the region.
What is the weather like in Serbia?
Serbia has four seasons.
Hot summers, from June to August.
Cold winters, with snow in the mountains.
Mild spring and colorful autumn.
The climate is good for farming and outdoor life.
What does Serbia look like?
Serbia has rivers like the Danube, one of the longest in Europe,
fertile plains in the north,
mountains and valleys in the south,
forests, lakes, and caves.
The nature is green, peaceful, and great for hiking.
What animals live in Serbia?
In Serbia, you can see foxes, deer, and hairs in the countryside.
Bears, wolves, and lynx in the mountains.
Eagles, owls, and storks in the sky.
Fish, frogs, and turtles, and rivers and lakes.
What do people eat in Serbia?
Serbian food is rich, flavorful, and meat-based.
People eat bread, cheese, and eggs.
Grilled meat, sausages, and stews.
Cabbage, beans, peppers, and potatoes.
Pastries and desserts.
Popular dishes.
Chivapi, small grilled meat rolls.
Sarma, cabbage rolls with meat and rice.
Gibonica, cheese pie with eggs and pastry.
Pausage, beans, stew, ivar, red pepper spread.
What do people drink in Serbia?
People drink.
Water and juice.
Coffee, strong and usually in small cups.
Tea, milk, and yogurt drinks.
Adults may drink rakia, a strong fruit brandy.
Also wine and beer.
Coffee and conversation are an important part of daily life.
What is life like in Serbia?
Life in Serbia is family-centered, social, and festive.
People enjoy, sitting in cafes, visiting family and friends,
going to music festivals, watching sports,
especially football and basketball.
Celebrating holidays with music and dancing.
What are some holidays and traditions?
Statehood Day, February 15.
Orthodox Christmas, January 7 Easter, with painted eggs and family gatherings.
Slava, a family saints' day.
Special to Serbian culture.
New Year, celebrated with fireworks and parties.
Traditional clothes, food, and folk dances are still part of many festivals.
Some fun facts about Serbia.
Serbia is home to the exit festival, one of Europe's biggest music events.
Nikola Tesla, the famous inventor, was born in this region.
The Serbian language uses both Latin and Cyrillic alphabets.
Serbia has over 15 natural spas.
The national flag is red, blue, and white with a double-headed eagle.
Now you know many things about Serbia.
You know where it is, what people eat, and how they live.
You learned about the rivers, mountains, and traditions.
Well done.
I am Emily.
Goodbye.
Or as they say in Serbian, dovigena.
